correctness.rationale: Spanning trees are in bijection with ordered path blocks with one selected spoke each; the single-block hub-leaf correction is explicit. A positive aperiodic rational renewal generating function has a unique dominant simple pole for each fixed positive weight. Implicit differentiation gives exact mean and variance densities and analytic quasi-powers yields the central limit theorem. Exact Sturm endpoint signs show that the degree-seven variance derivative has one zero on (0,1), establishing the unique global optimizer. The standalone standard-library checker matches independent exact spanning-tree enumeration at 28 parameter combinations and independently verifies the Sturm polynomial identity and signs. No finite experiment is treated as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The limiting leaf-count variance is a natural measure of structural uncertainty in spanning trees on a hub-and-path network. Conductance changes the random ensemble from path-dominated to star-dominated, forcing low fluctuation at both ends; the theorem proves, rather than guesses, the unique sharp intermediate optimum and supplies an exact leaf generating polynomial and Gaussian law. It is a motivated complete optimizer classification, not an arbitrary slice of a larger table.
